Spot premium quotations for imported cathode continued to decline in the follow-up to the Chinese Lunar New Year break as a result of a contraction in the SHFE/LME cash month price ratio. Upon re-opening after the week-long holiday, the SHFE price failed to track the rally in the LME price. Traders reported that the latest spot premium quotations for imported cathode were in the US$100-110/t range, whereas spot premium quotations for SXEW cathode were quoted at between US$90/t and $100/t. However, we have heard that very few deals have been © 2012 CRU International Limited **confidential** **February 2012** www.crugroup.com closed as consumers are reluctant to buy, with the domestic market not yet fully recovered from the holiday. We also heard reports of spot premiums for imported cathode to be used as collateral being quoted at around the $70/t mark. Imports of cathode for financing continue as credit availability remains tighter than expected by market insiders. We were told by market participants that cathode inventories in Shanghai bonded warehouses amounted to 330,000t350,000t at the time of writing, resulting from an increased in-flow during the week-long Lunar New Year holiday. According to Chinese customs data, China imported 406,937t of cathode in December 2011 - a record high. We expect cathode imports to decline in January as the SHFE/LME arbitrage remained negative since early January. # **China’s non-ferrous metals industry’s 12th five-year plan** As mentioned in the last fortnightly report, in this edition we will discuss China’s 12th five-year plan for the non-ferrous metals industry, which has been released by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, in more detail. The key aims of the plan include: developing a number of copper and nickel operations in coastal regions to process imported raw materials; consolidating metal recycling plants into several large-scale operations which would process domestic scrap copper and aluminum; encouraging the construction of alumina, aluminum, copper, lead, zinc and nickel industrial parks overseas. The plan also stressed the need to develop more production facilities for a number of higher value-added semis, including: copper alloy lead frames; high strength and high conductivity copp

er alloy wires; environmental friendly lead-free copper alloys; beryllium-free flexible high-performance copper alloys; highperformance corrosion resistant nickel-copper alloys; copper clad aluminum, high copper alloy sputtering palladium, rolled copper foil. In terms of copper resource exploration, the plan listed the names of some major copper mine projects, including: phase two of Yunnan Red Hill; phase two of the Inner Mongolia Wunugetushan ; Yunnan Pulang; Heilongjiang Duobaoshan; Jiangxi Zhushahong; Qinghai Deerni; Qinghai Tongyugou; Tibet Yulong; Tibet Jiama; Tibet Qulong polymetallic and Tibet Xietongmen. The plan also promotes the development of overseas copper mine projects in the resource-rich regions of Zambia, Congo, Peru, Afghanistan, Laos, Mongolia, Pakistan and Ecuador, among others. With regards to policy trends, the plan stated that the Chinese government will further regulate non-ferrous metal scrap import clearance orders and improve imported scrap clearance testing facilities. In addition, the government will also establish strategic non-ferrous metal reserve systems through a combination of national strategic reserves and commercial reserves , as well as considering the locations of mineral deposits. © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 4 **February 2012** www.crugroup.com # **Subdued appetite for copper after the Lunar New Year** The SHFE failed to follow the surge in the LME copper price after China’s Lunar New Year break, indicating subdued domestic demand for copper. We understand that semis fabricators are returning to the market gradually this week, however, most of them are demonstrating cautious buying behaviour, fuelled by pessimism over the copper price remaining at current high levels. We noticed that many semis fabricators’ capacity utilization was low this week and we expect them to fully return to the market after the Lantern Festival on 6th February. Wire and cable producers confirmed the view of weak Q1 demand, with few new orders expected to come from wirerod fabricators. Copper tube producers continue to struggle with the government’s withdrawal of home appliance stimulus policies. Copper plate, sheet and strip producers were of the opinion that demand will remain flat. We expect cathode demand to improve next week as more semis producers re-enter the market, however, for the remainder of the quarter, we expect demand to be somewhat subdued. # **Copper prices retreated** SHFE 3-month price

The LME 3-month price hit $8,623/t during China’s Lunar New Year break, as investors became more optimistic, with fewer negative news surrounding the Eurozone, the release of positive US corporate earnings and employment data, and expectations of improved credit availability in China.  However, the LME 3-month copper price retreated after China’s Lunar New Year break due to investors’ concerns over a possible Greek debt default and weaker demand from Chinese consumers.  The SHFE 3-month copper price fluctuated between 

RMB59,500/t and RMB60,620/t this week.  Moreover, the Shanghai physical market discount remained at RMB250-350/t.  According to the latest report, stocks in the SHFE cathode inventories surged to 179,891t this week, up 48,246t compared to two weeks ago.  All the figures above indicate that the copper price lacks sufficient momentum to continue the upward

The purchasing managers’ index (PMI) rose from 50.3 to 50.5 in December, based on figures from the National Bureau of Statistics of China and the China Federation of Logistics and Purchasing.  A reading above 50 indicates an expansion.  Some market insiders anticipate a reduced possibility of further credit loosening in the short term based on this PMI data.  In summary, we forecast that the SHFE 3-month copper price will fluctuate between RMB58,00060,000/t over the next two weeks given weak demand and abundant supply.
